operations.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin → Fragmented and primed
operations.description: Adapter-loaded Tn5 acts on accessible DNA within native chromatin, inserting adapter DNA while fragmenting the substrate. The insertion-bound illustration and subsequent Fragmented and primed illustration are consecutive depictions of this tagmentation transformation, not separate inferred enzyme reactions. The output is adapter-tagged genomic fragments, including material represented between nucleosome-bearing segments.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 transposition simultaneously fragments genomic DNA and transfers its sequencing-adapter payload. Less accessible chromatin is sterically less permissive, so recoverable amplifiable fragments are preferentially generated at accessible regions.
operations.information_effect: Physical carriers are adapter-tagged genomic DNA fragments. Their genomic sequence and insertion-associated ends preserve where accessible chromatin was sampled. This is preferential accessibility sampling, not a guarantee of exclusive recovery of biologically active regulatory elements or direct identification of a bound protein.

operations.mechanism: Purification recovers the tagged DNA and PCR amplifies library fragments using adapter-compatible primers. The schematic does not specify an internal cleanup sequence.
